chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Utterances are preserved and actions are to be tried.
Every soul, for what it earned, is held in pledge!
People are to be made deficient (as regards their bodies) and meddled with ( as regards their minds) except those whom Allāh protects.
The questioner among them aims at confusing and the answerer creates hardship.
It is possible that the man who has the best views among them will be deviated from the soundness of his thinking by pleasure or displeasure,
and it is possible that a single glance may affect even the man with the best wisdom among them or a single expression may transform him.
ai.seo_question: How does human emotion affect wisdom and steadfastness according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the inherent vulnerability of human nature, noting that while words are preserved and inner states are tested, most people are susceptible to external influences and internal emotions. He illustrates how even the wisest individuals can be swayed by pleasure or displeasure, and the most steadfast can be affected by a single glance or word, except for those protected by God. This reflection underscores the Shia concept of *'ismah* (divine protection) as the exception to the general rule of human fallibility and the need for spiritual vigilance against the distractions of the world.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 343. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Utterances are preserved and actions are to be tried.
Every soul, for what it earned, is held in pledge! (Qur’ān, 74:38).
People are to be made deficient (as regards their bodies) and meddled with (as regards their minds) except those whom Allāh protects.
The questioner among them aims at confusing and the answerer creates hardship.
It is possible that the man who has the best views among them will be deviated from the soundness of his thinking by pleasure or displeasure,
and it is possible that a single glance may affect even the man with the best wisdom among them or a single expression may transform him.
